posts.text:
In 1920 Hungary lost about two-thirds of its territory in a single treaty. In 1921 Hungarian propagandists answered by drawing what the same treaty would have done to France, Britain, Germany and the USA.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The Treaty of Trianon was signed on June 4, 1920 at the Grand Trianon palace at Versailles. The Kingdom of Hungary shrank from roughly 325,000 km² to about 93,000 km² — a loss of around 72% of its territory.

2/ Population fell from about 20.9 million to roughly 7.6 million. Around 3 million ethnic Hungarians ended up outside the new borders. That's the top-left panel: the actual treaty, drawn to the same scale as the hypotheticals.

3/ Romania took the largest single share in Transylvania. Czechoslovakia took Slovakia and Carpathian Ruthenia. Yugoslavia took Croatia-Slavonia and the Vojvodina. Austria received Burgenland. Poland and Italy took slices too.

4/ So the map asks: what if it were you? France reduced to a core with Britain, Germany, Italy and Spain carved out of it. The USA left with a central strip while Japan, the UK, Mexico and Spain hold the rest.

5/ The British panel is the most pointed of the set — England cut back to the south, the USA holding Ireland, Germany holding the north. The implied argument isn't subtle: you would call this intolerable.

6/ The slogan attached to the campaign was “Nem, nem, soha!” — “No, no, never!” Border revision dominated Hungarian politics for the next two decades and shaped which side the country ended up on in 1939.

7/ Worth being clear about what this isn't: neutral cartography. It was built to manufacture grievance. Which is exactly what makes it useful for understanding interwar Europe.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
